_comment: Long sentences broken into shorter ones, in two batches, applied by
`.freebuff/tmp/split_apply.py` (verified against the file, refusing any edit whose
`old` is ambiguous or whose span has markup inside it):
python .freebuff/tmp/split_apply.py data/sentence_splits.json          # dry run
python .freebuff/tmp/split_apply.py data/sentence_splits.json --apply
The FIRST batch is the eleven entries plan.md records, applied with the older
`.freebuff/tmp/apply_edits.py`: nine are in force and two were withdrawn, because
ch2's and ch9's first candidates sat inside a passage the voice catalogue had
already rewritten. tools/voice_rewrite.py records the exact replacement text, so a
later pass must not edit text inside one of those: the split reports 'a rewritten
passage has been reverted' and takes the chapter out of the gate.
The SECOND batch is the pass that followed the reader's 'these content seem hard'
against the corrected measurement (tools/sentence_length.py now breaks on block
boundaries and excludes quotations, so the real figure was 105 sentences over 45
words rather than 149): about 120 splits across all nine units, which took the
count to 3.
Those 3 are not an oversight. Each is a sentence whose ENTIRE text is a recorded
voice rewrite, so there is no split inside it that leaves the record intact:
* ch2 2.3.7  'The diagrams carry five ideas: ...' (78 words)
* ch2 2.4.1  'Sockets are built up in this order: ...' (64 words)
* ch8 8.4.4  'The boundary between provider and customer is drawn differently
for each service model, since ... or the reverse.' (48 words)
They are named here rather than worked around. Splitting one means a superseding
entry in data/voice_rewrites.json, applied through voice_rewrite.py --apply so its
fingerprints and indexes stay replayable - a decision about the voice record rather
than about the prose, and not one to make inside a length pass.
The THIRD batch is the pass against tools/sentence_length.py's post-rewrite count:
fifteen prose sentences over 45 words had reappeared as units 4-8 were rewritten, and
this batch splits all of them. Two needed the catalogue rather than a split: ch2 2.3.7
is a whole-sentence voice rewrite, retired with `tools/voice_rewrite.py --retire` so
the length pass could touch it, and data/dcc_figure_keepers.json's ch2 prose patch was
re-pointed at the split sentence. ch3 3.1's split first dropped the pinned term
'logical clocks' and was rewritten to keep it (the Revise-card guard caught it). After
this batch the count over 45 words is 0; the measured longest is 45.
